messages:
Maya (Marketing): quick huddle: we need a differentiated battlecard that leans into migration risk reduction + cost transparency vs clouds and DIY infra. short + rep-ready.
Leo (Marketing Ops): can we make a 2-slide "migration play" that SDRs can drop into outreach? one slide for value prop, one slide for procurement/ops talking points.
Sam (Sales): yes — reps want a 1-line opener, a 45s discovery script, and a single pricing rebuttal. less fluff.
Noor (Product Marketing): angle suggestion: "risk-managed migration" — emphasize predictable fallbacks, automated rollbacks, and a verified cost delta per workload. buyers hate surprise bills.
Priya (Research): bench blurb I'll provide: workload-level comparison (chat vs long-context batch vs embedding pipelines). show cost/token delta and p95 tail behavior. will keep methods terse.
Owen (Field): add an ops checklist: network egress, private endpoint patterns, KMS, audit retention. also include a short note on vendor exit: how customers export model traces & logs. procurement loves escape hatches.
Maya (Marketing): deliverables: 1) 1-liner + 45s script 2) migration play 2-slide PDF 3) 3 quick competitor zingers 4) webinar concept: "Migration without the jitters" 5) 3 subject-line variants. owners?
Sam (Sales): I'll own 1 + 3 (sales copy + zingers). will post drafts by EOD.
Owen (Field): I'll draft ops checklist + vendor-exit note.
Priya (Research): sending a short methods & table (p95 + cost delta) in-thread in ~90m. will include the exact knob settings we used.
Noor (Product Marketing): webinar plan idea: 20-min customer story (anonymized) + 25-min migration runbook (live) + 15-min Q&A. call it: "Migration without the jitters: a playbook."
launch-bot: Webinar tentative slot: 2024-09-10 16:00 UTC  calendar hold placed.
Maya (Marketing): sample 1-liner draft: 
"Redwood Inference: reduce inference surprises — predictable costs, fallback-safe rollouts, and ops controls that make migrations low-risk."
Sam (Sales): 45s discovery script draft: 
"Quick question: when you ramp model traffic, do you see cost variance or unexpected latency spikes? We help teams lock unit economics and provide rollback paths so migrations don't become fires to fight."
Noor (Product Marketing): competitor zingers (draft):
- vs cloud AI: "They scale your model; we stabilize your bill and SLAs for production traffic."
- vs LLM APIs: "We match API ergonomics but add private deploy & exit guarantees."
- vs infra vendors: "No brittle glue code — a verified runtime, control plane, and migration runbook out of the box."
Leo (Marketing Ops): subject lines to A/B test:
A) "Migrate your LLMs without surprise bills"
B) "How to avoid inference chaos during model rollouts"
C) "Migration playbook: predictable costs + safe rollouts"
Sam (Sales): I'll test A/B on SDR list; track CTR and replies.
Maya (Marketing): ops: please draft the 2-slide migration play (Leo), attach the ops checklist (Owen), and Priya drop the bench table. I'll assemble PDF + short landing copy.
Priya (Research): posting a compact table and methods note in-thread in ~70m. minimal text, numbers only.
Owen (Field): confirming a potential anonymized customer for the story; need legal review. ETA tomorrow.
Maya (Marketing): timeline: lock all assets in this thread by next Tue so we can sync with enablement. owners recap: Sam (sales lines + zingers), Leo (play slide + subject lines), Priya (bench methods & table), Owen (ops checklist + case stub), Noor (webinar format + runbook), Maya (assemble + landing). reopen if blockers. :triangular_flag_on_post:
